---
title: Runtime Config
description: Describe your cluster once, reuse it across training recipes
---

A runtime config is a small YAML file describing *where and how* training is
launched — launcher choice, cluster resources, rendezvous details — separate
from the training recipe, which describes *what* is trained. Pass it with
`--runtime`:

```bash
axolotl train recipe.yaml --runtime cluster.yaml
```

The same runtime file is reusable across recipes and, by design, contains no
per-node state (no machine ranks, no node counts): the identical file works on
every node of a cluster. Example files live in
[`examples/runtime/`](https://github.com/axolotl-ai-cloud/axolotl/tree/main/examples/runtime).

## Schema

```bash
axolotl config-schema --runtime   # full JSON schema
```

```yaml
launcher: ray        # accelerate | torchrun | ray | python
                     # optional when exactly one launcher block is present

env:                 # env vars applied to the launch (any launcher)
  NCCL_DEBUG: WARN

ray:
  address: null            # omit: use an `axolotl ray up`/`ray start` cluster if running,
                           #   else an isolated local instance (concurrent runs stay independent)
                           # auto/ray://…: attach to a running cluster
                           # http(s)://host:8265: submit via the Ray Jobs API
  num_workers: auto        # or an int; auto = derived from total cluster resources
  resources_per_worker:
    GPU: 1
    # accelerator_type:H100: 0.001   # pin a GPU type
  run_name: my-run
  detach: false            # Jobs API: return after submitting
  runtime_env:             # Ray runtime_env (Jobs uploads, worker env)
    working_dir: .
    excludes: ["outputs/"]
    pip: ["some-extra-dep"]
    env_vars:
      HF_HOME: /mnt/shared/hf
  cluster:                 # consumed by `axolotl ray up/down/status`
    hostfile: ./hostfile
    ssh_user: ubuntu
    head_port: 6379
    dashboard_port: 8265

torchrun:
  nnodes: 2                # int or elastic range "1:4"
  nproc_per_node: 8        # int, or auto/gpu/cpu
  rdzv_backend: c10d
  rdzv_endpoint: 10.0.0.4:29400
  rdzv_id: my-run
  master_addr: 10.0.0.4
  master_port: 29500

accelerate:
  num_processes: 16
  num_machines: 2
  main_process_ip: 10.0.0.4
  main_process_port: 29500
  config_file: ./accelerate.yaml
  mixed_precision: bf16
```

`machine_rank`/`node_rank` are deliberately not part of the schema — they
differ per node. Use rendezvous-based launching (torchrun c10d, or Ray, which
needs no ranks at all), or pass them per node after `--`:

```bash
axolotl train recipe.yaml --runtime cluster.yaml -- --machine_rank 1
```

## Precedence

From strongest to weakest:

1. Explicit CLI flags (`--launcher`, `--ray-num-workers`, …)
2. The `--runtime` file
3. Legacy keys in the training YAML (`use_ray: true`)
4. Default: `accelerate`

Arguments after `--` are passed to the launcher verbatim and override any
matching flag derived from the runtime file.

## The three Ray flows

**In-cluster driver** — run on a machine that is (or can start) a Ray cluster:

```bash
axolotl train recipe.yaml --runtime examples/runtime/ray-single-node.yaml
```

With no `address`, axolotl uses the cluster brought up by `axolotl ray up` (or
any `ray start` cluster) when one is running, and an isolated local Ray
instance otherwise — concurrent trainings on one machine never interfere.
`num_workers: auto` uses every GPU that satisfies `resources_per_worker`. No
ranks, no host lists — adding nodes to the Ray cluster is all it takes to
scale.

**Ray Jobs submission** — run from anywhere, no SSH to the head node:

```bash
axolotl train recipe.yaml --runtime examples/runtime/ray-jobs-remote.yaml
```

When `address` is `http(s)://…:8265`, axolotl stages the recipe (plus
`runtime_env.working_dir` if set), submits via the Ray Jobs API, and streams
logs until completion. Ctrl-C stops the job unless `detach: true`.

**Cluster bring-up** — for bare-metal nodes without an existing Ray setup:

```bash
axolotl ray up --hostfile hostfile   # on the head node
axolotl ray status
axolotl ray down
```

`up` starts a head locally and joins each hostfile worker over passwordless
ssh; the cluster is recorded under `~/.cache/axolotl/` so `down` and `status`
need no arguments. See [Ray integration](ray-integration.qmd) for details.

## torchrun and accelerate

The `torchrun:` and `accelerate:` blocks replace hand-assembled `--`
passthrough for multi-node runs. A two-node torchrun setup becomes a file you
copy to both nodes and launch identically:

```bash
axolotl train recipe.yaml --runtime examples/runtime/torchrun-2node.yaml
```

If only `rdzv_endpoint` is set, axolotl fills in `rdzv_backend: c10d` and a
generated `rdzv_id`, matching the existing `--` passthrough behavior.
